svg.title: EMORI architecture: the robot as a native ROS 2 component
svg.desc: The hostapp chain on the left reaches the robot through a REST shim inside the robot node. The robot node owns Pollen's backend in-process: a motion arbiter with three lanes, actions and services, state publishers, perception streams and a lifecycle that parks the robot on shutdown. The EMORI ROS4HRI graph runs in the same container and sends skills to the node natively as action goals. Below: the hardware, an off-robot analytics consumer, any ROS 2 tool reading standard messages, and the in-process face look-at component.

the backend's state feeds the publishers

an outside tool subscribes to standard messages
the signals reach the engagement node
skills become action goals on the robot node

the hostapp historises to the off-robot broker
